title: Interpreting Topic Models in Byte-Pair Encoding Space
venue: Proceedings of the 31st International Conference on Computational Linguistics (COLING 2025)
task: Recovering and evaluating word-level topics from BPE token distributions
problem: Topics learned over BPE tokens contain word fragments, so word-based coherence measures cannot be applied.
architecture: Model-agnostic, training-free recovery: valid words are ranked from a topic-token distribution using aggregation of their tokens' probabilities (sum, mean, geometric mean, harmonic mean) and heuristics extending harmonic mean (RPS, RST); recovered topics evaluated with NPMI and topic uniqueness, compared with topics trained on original vocabularies; user study.
baselines: CombinedTM (topic models trained on BPE vs original vocabularies)
key_results: User study (10 participants): 82.6% of responses judged recovered BPE topics coherent vs 91.3% for topics from the original vocabulary.
Recovered topics are similar to original-vocabulary topics (duplication no worse than between different model classes); harmonic mean and RST recommended.
strengths: Opens topic modelling directly on LLM tokenisations (smaller vocabularies, less preprocessing).
Large corpora and four model families.

limitations.text: Only LLaMA's BPE tokenizer tested; results may depend on the tokenizer.
On small OCTIS corpora neural models (ProdLDA, CTM) collapse to a few topics in BPE space.
